steps.title: Welcome to your office
steps.body: You're the HCM for the Office of Learning Operations, for one full week. Requests come to you through the day, and on pay day you'll see what every decision did to someone's check. This tour takes about a minute.

steps.title: Game time
steps.body: It's Monday morning, Oct 19. Time moves while you work, 8:00 AM to 6:00 PM on weekdays. In Training mode, the clock pauses while you have a request open, so take your time reading. When you're caught up, time speeds up until the next request arrives.

steps.title: Your deadlines
steps.body: Straight from the 2026 payroll calendars. Backdated changes close at Wednesday's Retro Change Cutoff, other changes at Friday's HCM transaction cutoff, and time cards are due Monday at noon. The two on screen count down, turning amber inside the last workday and red inside the last 4 hours.

steps.title: Four meters
steps.body: Your decisions move these. Each shows an icon, a number, and a label.

steps.title: Your inbox
steps.body: New requests land here, with a count of unread items. Filter by topic, and sort by due time, newest, or priority. Quick questions are short chats from colleagues. Some messages are just FYI.

steps.title: Places in the office
steps.body: Jump to a spot in the office. A pin and a number mean something is waiting there. You can also click people and places in the 3D office.

steps.title: What the symbols mean
steps.body: Icons above people's heads show who needs you. Hover over a person to see the label.

steps.title: Your controls
steps.body: Every button is labeled. Here's what each one does.

steps.title: Try one
steps.body: Here's a practice request. It isn't scored. Pick an answer, press Decide, and read the feedback. In the real week, asking Renee for a hint costs 2 points.

steps.title: You're ready
steps.body: The clock starts when you close this. Open your inbox to begin. Press Help any time to see the symbols and controls again.

meters.label: Accuracy
meters.text: Are people paid the right amount? Higher is better.

meters.label: Risk
meters.text: Policy and wage law exposure. Lower is better.

meters.label: Trust
meters.text: How employees feel about their pay, and about you. Higher is better.

meters.label: Managers
meters.text: How managers feel about working with you. Higher is better.

symbols.label: Wants to talk
symbols.text: This person has a request for you. Click them, or open it from your inbox.

symbols.label: Time card issue
symbols.text: This person's time card has an exception you haven't handled yet.

symbols.label: Resolved
symbols.text: You handled this person's time card issue the right way.

symbols.label: Something is waiting here
symbols.text: A gold ring pulses on the floor where a request is waiting.

controls.label: Skip
controls.text: Jump ahead to the next request. Handy when you're caught up.

controls.label: Pause
controls.text: Stop the clock. Press again to resume.

controls.label: Zoom
controls.text: Zoom the 3D office out or in.

controls.label: View
controls.text: Switch between the 3D office and List view. Same game, no 3D needed.

controls.label: Binder
controls.text: The Policy Binder: the policies behind every decision, searchable.

controls.label: Voices
controls.text: Turns character voices on or off. Captions always show, so you never need sound.

controls.label: Settings
controls.text: Clock speed (including Manual), text size, reduced motion, and view.

controls.label: Help
controls.text: This guide: the symbols, the controls, and the tour.

practice.title: Practice: where deadlines live
practice.context: Renee: "Quick warm-up before the clock starts. This one isn't scored."
practice.intro: Quick warm-up before the clock starts. This one isn't scored.
practice.hint: Dates move with weekends, holidays, and year end. Where would you check every time?

decision.prompt: Where do you check the deadlines for a pay period?

choices.feedback: Right. The payroll calendar is the source of truth, because dates move with weekends, holidays, and year end. That's how every decision works here: pick one, press Decide, and read the feedback.

choices.text: Whatever the dates were last period
choices.feedback: Dates move with weekends, holidays, and year end, so last period's dates can be wrong. Check the payroll calendar every period. In the real game, a wrong answer like this costs points and can show up on pay day.

choices.text: Ask a coworker when things are due
choices.feedback: A coworker might remember wrong. The payroll calendar is the source of truth. In the real game, a wrong answer like this costs points and can show up on pay day.
